summary: The biggest new integrity risk appeared today. On 16 Oct a public commit (branch claude/fervent-edison-sqk1ry, 412e9e3) dropped the team's old 'AI never writes deliverables' rule. It now lets Claude edit the IPS, Trading Notes and Final Report as '[AI]' Google Docs suggestions, and 13 AI rewrites of IPS V5 sentences are already drafted and public. Wharton's rule is 'You may not submit any work generated by an AI program as your own'. The IPS cannot carry citations, so any AI sentence accepted into it goes in with no credit at all. Second, a public fork of the repo was created on 15 Oct. GitHub says public forks 'stay public' when the parent goes private, so the 15 Oct fix of 'make the repo private' is no longer enough on its own: the fork must be deleted first. Third, the rule covers AI 'work', not only words. The strategy idea, the models, the numbers and the charts were largely AI-built, and the record says the team 'deferred to the assistant's calls'. All of that must be credited in the Works Cited, and students must be able to rebuild and defend the key numbers, especially at the semifinal. My measurements put IPS V5 at the end of an AI draft chain: shared phrases with the AI exemplar fall 89% -> 63% -> 34% -> 18%, and V5 shares 71% with the AI-voiced Tab 15. That is a rewording pattern, not proof of student authorship, so a fresh student draft is still required. Other items: the routines call the AI 'the consultant for Team Caplet', next to a rule that disqualifies teams suspected of using paid 'consultants ... or other agents' (low odds but easy to fix). An AI agent operated WInS on 7 Oct, the 'AI may fill a ticket up to Preview' rule is still in place, and Stock-Trak's terms ban robots. False or template AI records remain (a '100% by students' statement and 242 mock log rows), and the real AI log jumps from 30 Sep to 16 Oct. Smaller items: title-page names must match the roster exactly or the IPS is 'not considered', COMPETITION.md still calls Laura fictional, the school letter has not been requested, and the WInS username is still exposed. Nothing found is yet a proven breach of a disqualification rule. The serious risks only become real if AI text or uncredited AI analysis is submitted, and all the fixes are cheap if done this weekend.

findings.problem: Ray's 16 Oct rule replaces 'do not write the deliverables' with AI-tagged suggestions on the IPS, Trading Notes and Final Report, relying on later Works Cited credit. The IPS bans citations, so accepted AI sentences would be submitted uncredited and judged as the team's 'authentic voice'. The public history shows the stricter rule was knowingly relaxed. AI text edited by AI on top of an AI-generated V5.
